--- a/minbpe/regex.py
+++ b/minbpe/regex.py
@@ -310,5 +310,31 @@
-                new = list(new)
-                s = b"\xff".join(map(str.encode, new)).decode("latin-1")

+                new = list(new)
+                s = b"\xff".join(map(str.encode, new)).decode("latin-1")
+                # every few merges, chunks that no pending merge can touch
+                # (one token, or a pair that is merged earlier or never) are
+                # taken out of s, so later replace scans are shorter
+                out = [None] * len(new)
+                live = range(len(new))
+                rank_get = self._enc_state[5].get
+                n = len(table)
+                step = 64
+                for start in range(0, n, step):
+                    stop = start + step
+                    for ps, c in table[start:stop]:
+                        s = s.replace(ps, c)
+                    if stop >= n:
+                        break
+                    keep = []
+                    kapp = keep.append
+                    parts = []
+                    papp = parts.append
+                    for k, p in zip(live, s.split("\xff")):
+                        if len(p) < 2 or (len(p) == 2 and rank_get(p, -1) < stop):
+                            out[k] = p
+                        else:
+                            kapp(k)
+                            papp(p)
+                    live = keep
+                    s = "\xff".join(parts)
+                for k, p in zip(live, s.split("\xff")):
+                    out[k] = p
+                cache.update(zip(new, [list(map(ord, p)) for p in out]))

I ran no sandbox evaluations, so I have no measured result for that edit. The session stopped without submitting a candidate. Nothing I changed has been tested.

I do not yet know whether my rewrite there is correct or faster. Expanding 5 lines into 31 without a measurement is a guess, not progress.

Next session I should first run lineage_bench.py on the unmodified code to get a baseline. Then I should re-apply or rethink the regex.py edit and measure it against that baseline. If it does not clearly help, I should drop it rather than submit it untested.
